source.title: Unsupervised Neural Machine Translation with Generative Language Models Only
source.authors: Jesse Michael Han; Igor Babuschkin; Harrison Edwards; Arvind Neelakantan; Tao Xu; Stanislas Polu; Alex Ray; Pranav Shyam; A. Ramesh; A. Radford; I. Sutskever

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It reports translation BLEU across model sizes, which bears on downstream performance versus scale, but it does not measure held-out pretraining loss or fit scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The study reports downstream BLEU by GPT-3 model size. It does not test loss scaling, small-run extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, or architecture-shape effects. Scaling-law works are cited as background; no loss or compute-optimal results from those citations are recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: An unsupervised machine-translation method paper. Tables 1, 2 and 5 report WMT14 en-fr/fr-en test BLEU across GPT-3 family sizes. Table 5 extends from 125M to 175B for the plain pretrained models (zero-shot and self-amplified prompting). These bear only on V6's direction, whether downstream BLEU rises with size. The study fits no curve, measures no pretraining loss and makes no claim about predictability. The fine-tuned series (Tables 1, 2) cover only 125M to 1.3B, about one order of magnitude, and are the study's own pipeline.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that generative LMs alone can implement the full unsupervised NMT pipeline (few-shot amplification, distillation, backtranslation), reaching 42.1 BLEU on WMT14 en-fr. GPT-3 bootstrap samples 'saturate' the smaller models, meaning they gain little from backtranslation. Mixing in CC100 monotext adds about 3 BLEU at all scales. They draw no conclusions about scaling laws.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares downstream translation BLEU across GPT-3 family sizes and training procedures; it does not measure held-out language-model loss, fit power laws, or vary compute-optimal parameter/token allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: Model-size trends depend on bootstrap and training condition: self-distilled versus GPT-3-generated bootstrap samples, backtranslation, and the addition of CC100 monolingual data. Zero-shot French-to-English results are non-monotonic across some sizes.
record.problems: BLEU is a downstream translation metric rather than held-out pretraining loss; no scaling-law fit or uncertainty estimates are reported. Comparisons vary training stage and data condition as well as model size.
record.rows_left_out: The remaining phase-by-phase BLEU results in Tables 1, 2, 5, 6, 7, and 8, including initial distillation/backtranslation, alternative few-shot examples, and demonstration-count conditions, are omitted; this record retains the final-stage model-size comparisons and the Table 2 distillation results relevant to V6. Table 3's comparisons to prior work are not rows because they are not this study's own model-size intervention results.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
No fitted law and no extrapolation from small runs.
No architecture-shape variation at fixed parameter count.
No power-law fit in fine-tuning or other regimes; only BLEU at a handful of sizes.
Predictability is untested: there is no fit of BLEU to size or to pretraining loss, and no forecast of larger models. Only the direction of change across 4 to 5 sizes is reported.
No comparison of exponents or fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: Rows r1-r32 measure the study's own fine-tuned pipeline across sizes, with training stage and data confounded. They are weaker evidence on V6 than the pure pretrained-model series. Table 1's few-shot (tau=0) rows (1.15, 7.71, 13.07, 14.28 en-fr) and Table 6's real-example series also rise with size. These are declared in rows_left_out but would be the cleaner pretrained-model evidence if rows were added. No uncertainty is reported; single runs.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether power laws fitted on smaller runs predict larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Effects of depth, width, and architecture at fixed parameter count.
Power-law forms in other modalities or training regimes.
The study reports BLEU across model sizes, not whether downstream performance is predictable from pretraining loss or a fitted scaling law.
Dependence of scaling exponents or compute-optimal allocation on fit choices, and curve bending.

relationships.condition: Fine-tuned pipeline after iterative backtranslation (self-distilled, GPT-3 bootstrap, +CC100), 125M to 1.3B
relationships.reason: Final BLEU rises monotonically with size in both directions in every condition, e.g. en-fr 30.48 to 39.12 (r1-r8, r17-r32). The span is only about one order of magnitude.
relationships.display_finding: Final BLEU increased monotonically in both translation directions under every tested pipeline condition, including English-to-French from 30.48 to 39.12 over roughly one order of magnitude in model size.

relationships.condition: Pretrained models with self-amplified few-shot prompting, 125M to 175B (Table 5)
relationships.reason: BLEU rises monotonically at every size in both directions: en-fr 1.39 to 29.96, fr-en 5.76 to 31.75 (r43-r52).
relationships.display_finding: BLEU increased at every tested size in both directions, from 1.39 to 29.96 for English-to-French and 5.76 to 31.75 for French-to-English.

relationships.reason: fr-en is non-monotonic: medium 13.92 is above large 8.14 (r36, r38). en-fr stays near 0 to 3 BLEU up to 1.3B, then jumps to 26.19 at 175B (r33, r35, r37, r39, r41).
relationships.display_finding: With zero-shot prompting, French-to-English BLEU falls from 13.92 at medium to 8.14 at large, while English-to-French stays around 0–3 through 1.3B before jumping to 26.19 at 175B.

relationships.condition: Distillation on GPT-3 self-amplified samples (Table 2), en-fr
relationships.reason: BLEU plateaus between large and xl (37.21 vs 37.08), while fr-en rises throughout (r9-r16).
relationships.display_finding: With distillation on GPT-3 self-amplified samples, English-to-French BLEU plateaus from 37.21 at large to 37.08 at xl, while French-to-English improves throughout.
